text:
A language with no relatives?

The Yuchi (YOO-chee), also called Euchee, call themselves Tsoyaha (tso-YAH-hah), “Children of the Sun.” Their language is an isolate. Linguists have not demonstrated a relationship to any other family. Proposals of a distant link to Siouan, and sometimes to a larger Macro-Siouan grouping that would also include Iroquoian and Caddoan, have been offered by scholars including the linguist Edward Sapir, the linguist Mary Haas, and the linguist Robert Rankin. Those proposals rest on a limited set of possible cognates and on morphological parallels such as classifiers and certain verb patterns. Most specialists still treat the language as an isolate because regular sound correspondences have not been established.

In the oral tradition the Sun is mother. In one version documented in the Tuggle collection, the world was covered by water. Animals brought up earth and the Sun provided light. A drop of her blood fell to the ground and the first people sprang from that place. They were the children of the Sun. 

Another migration legend, collected by the anthropologist Frank Speck in 1904 from Ekilarne Cahwee (also called Lewis Long), tells of a split. One group went west over the mountains. Those who remained were the Tsoyaha.

At the time of first European contact, the Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto met them in 1541 in the eastern Tennessee River valley. He recorded them as the Uchi, associated with the Chisca. They lived then in the ridge and valley country of what is now eastern Tennessee and neighboring areas. Pressure from the Cherokee later pushed them south. By the late 17th and early 18th centuries they occupied towns in present-day Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina, often near or within the Creek Confederacy while keeping their own language and identity.

In 1714 Cherokees, encouraged by English traders, destroyed the Yuchi town of Chestowee in present-day Bradley County, Tennessee. The Yuchi traded deerskins with colonial settlers and took part in the regional slave trade. During the Creek War of 1813 to 1814 many sided with the traditionalist Red Sticks. In the 1830s the United States removed them westward with the Muscogee (Creek). 

They settled near Sapulpa in Indian Territory. The Dawes Commission later listed them as Creek. They have never received separate federal recognition. An independent petition was denied in 2000. Many are enrolled citizens of the Muscogee Nation.

They continue to maintain three ceremonial grounds and to hold the Green Corn ceremony. Their language marks Yuchi people differently from non-Yuchi people. That distinction is built into the grammar itself.

The last widely known first-language speaker, the elder Maxine Wildcat Barnett (golaha, “grandmother”), died on August 27, 2021. She had worked for years with the Yuchi Language Project, founded in the 1990s by Richard A. Grounds, Ph.D. (Yuchi name shUpa). The project operates a full-day immersion school that currently serves about 30 students from preschool through fifth grade. For the first time in nearly a century, children are speaking Yuchi as a mother tongue at home, at school, and at the ceremonial grounds. Parents are raising babies in the language. Roughly 50 people now speak it at varying levels of fluency. The Yuchi people are still here.

text:
A Berean Synthesis: The Whole Counsel on Dispensationalism
A true Berean examination (Acts 17:11) searches the Scriptures to test whether a doctrinal system harmonizes with the whole counsel of God.
Dispensationalism—originating in the 1830s under John Nelson Darby and popularized by the Scofield Reference Bible—rests on a fundamental premise: God maintains two distinct peoples with separate programs, separate covenants, and separate destinies (earthly Israel and the heavenly Church). To sustain this separation, the system uses a flat, literalistic hermeneutic that separates Law from Grace, inserts an unprophesied gap into prophetic timelines, and postpones the Davidic Kingdom to an earthly millennium.
When tested against inspired apostolic interpretation, all 15 foundational premises of dispensationalism resolve into five structural pillars. Below is the direct cross-examination of each pillar, contrasting the dispensational claim against the clear testimony of the written Word.
Pillar 1: The Hermeneutic (Literalism vs. Apostolic Typology)
The Dispensational Claim
Prophecy and Old Testament promises must be interpreted with uniform, literalistic flatness. Treating national, territorial, or sacrificial promises as fulfilled spiritually or corporately in Christ is rejected as illicit "allegorizing" or "replacement theology."
The Scriptural Cross-Examination
The Apostles never practiced flat literalism; they interpreted the Old Testament through Christological Typology. Physical Old Covenant institutions were earthly shadows (skia) intentionally designed to point to their substance (sōma) in Jesus Christ:
Colossians 2:16–17 & Hebrews 10:1: The Law, festivals, new moons, and sacrifices were shadows; the physical substance belongs exclusively to Christ.
Matthew 2:15 (quoting Hosea 11:1): Hosea literally referred to national Israel coming out of Egypt ("out of Egypt have I called my son"), yet Matthew reveals that Jesus Christ is the True Israel. Where the ethnic nation failed, the singular Son fulfilled the type.
Romans 4:13 & Hebrews 11:10–16: The localized geographic grant of Canaan was a temporary earthly type. In Christ, the promise to Abraham was expanded to inherit the entire cosmos (kosmos), pointing forward to the New Heavens and New Earth.
Berean Verdict: Insisting that physical shadows must be fulfilled in their earthly, temporal forms diminishes the finished work of Christ. The Apostles did not spiritualize promises away—they demonstrated that every Old Testament type finds its climactic fulfillment in the Person of Jesus.
Pillar 2: The People of God (Two Separate Programs vs. One New Man)
The Dispensational Claim
God maintains two eternally distinct entities: ethnic Israel (earthly) and the Church (heavenly). The Church is an unprophesied "mystery parenthesis" created after Israel rejected the kingdom. Furthermore, Genesis 12:3 mandates unconditional geopolitical blessing based on biological descent from Jacob.
The Scriptural Cross-Examination
The New Testament explicitly refutes the idea of parallel tracks, declaring that the Cross permanently demolished the dividing wall:
Ephesians 2:14–16: Christ did not maintain two separate peoples; He broke down the wall of partition to make of the two "one new man" (hena kainon anthrōpon) reconciled in "one body."
Galatians 3:16, 28–29: The promises were made to Abraham and his singular Seed: Christ. Therefore, anyone belonging to Christ—whether Jew or Gentile—is legally, spiritually, and covenantally Abraham's seed and an heir according to the promise.
Romans 11:16–24 (The Single Olive Tree): Paul presents only one domestic Olive Tree of faith. Unbelieving ethnic branches are broken off; believing Gentiles are grafted into the same root; repentant Jews are grafted back into their own tree. Scripture knows nothing of two parallel trees.
Romans 9:6–8 & Galatians 6:15–16: "They are not all Israel, which are of Israel." True Jewish identity and the "Israel of God" are defined by the New Creation and regeneration of the heart, not genetic pedigree (Romans 2:28–29; Philippians 3:3).
Galatians 3:8–14 (Genesis 12:3 Defined): The "blessing of Abraham" is explicitly defined as justification by faith and the gift of the Spirit in Christ, not a geopolitical foreign-policy mandate for secular nations.
Berean Verdict: God has only ever had one redeemed body. Biological lineage confers zero spiritual advantage before God. In Christ, ethnic barriers are obliterated into the singular household of faith.
Pillar 3: Covenants and the Kingdom (Postponed vs. Inaugurated)
The Dispensational Claim
When national Israel rejected Jesus, the promised Davidic Kingdom was suspended and postponed until a future earthly millennium. Consequently, Christ is currently seated only on the Father's throne in heaven, not on the Throne of David. Furthermore, the New Covenant belongs strictly to ethnic Israel, with the Church participating only as secondary beneficiaries.
The Scriptural Cross-Examination
The Apostles taught that the Kingdom was inaugurated and the Davidic Covenant fulfilled through Christ’s resurrection and ascension:
Acts 2:29–36: Peter explicitly proclaims that David foretold the resurrection of Christ as the exact event that seated Him upon David's throne. Christ is reigning as King of kings now.
Acts 15:13–18 (quoting Amos 9:11–12): James settles the Jerusalem Council by declaring that the incorporation of Gentiles into the Church is the rebuilding of the fallen Tabernacle of David.
Colossians 1:13 & Matthew 12:28: Believers are not waiting for a future millennium to enter the kingdom; they have already been "translated into the kingdom of his dear Son."
Luke 22:20 & Hebrews 8:6–13: Christ enacted the New Covenant in His blood, and the author of Hebrews directly quotes Jeremiah 31:31 to confirm that individual regenerate believers—who organically constitute the true assembly (ekklēsia), the living body of Christ—are the actual participants and ministers of this very covenant (2 Corinthians 3:3, 6). The New Covenant is not established with an earthly religious institution, denomination, or visible hierarchy, but is written directly by the Holy Spirit onto the mind and heart of every redeemed individual.
Berean Verdict: The Kingdom was not postponed, nor was the Church a backup plan. Christ is presently reigning on the Davidic Throne over His spiritual house, mediating the New Covenant for all believers.
Pillar 4: Temple, Sacrifices, and the Law (Shadows vs. The Finished Sacrifice)
The Dispensational Claim
Classical dispensationalism anticipates a literal rebuilt third temple in Jerusalem during the millennium, complete with animal blood sacrifices (Ezekiel 40–48), while creating sharp administrative divides between the era of Mosaic Law and the era of Grace.
The Scriptural Cross-Examination
Scripture teaches one continuous way of salvation and forbids any return to animal sacrifices:
Romans 4:1–8 & Galatians 3:6–9: Salvation has always been exclusively by grace through faith in the Messiah. Abraham (before the Law) and David (under the Law) were justified by imputed righteousness, never by legal works.
Hebrews 8:13; 10:11–18: The Mosaic administration was made obsolete and vanished away at Calvary. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever and sat down. To reintroduce animal blood sacrifices—even as "memorials"—directly contradicts the Holy Spirit's declaration: "Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin."
1 Corinthians 3:16 & Ephesians 2:20–22: The physical stone temple in Jerusalem has been superseded by the true Temple: the living body of Christ, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets.
Berean Verdict: A return to physical animal blood sacrifices in an earthly temple reverses redemptive history and diminishes the absolute finality of Christ's cross.
Pillar 5: Eschatology and Daniel's 70th Week (Single Consummation vs. Secret Split)
The Dispensational Claim
Daniel 9:24–27 contains an unmentioned 2,000-year gap between the 69th and 70th week. During this gap, the Church resides in a parenthesis until an "imminent, signless" secret Rapture removes them, restarting the final seven years of tribulation for Israel prior to a second public coming.
The Scriptural Cross-Examination
Scripture presents a unified prophetic timeline centered on Christ and a single, climactic Day of the Lord:
Daniel 9:24–27: The prophecy declares seventy continuous weeks determined to make reconciliation for iniquity and bring in everlasting righteousness. Messiah the Prince confirmed the New Covenant with "the many" (Matthew 26:28) and caused animal sacrifices to cease by His once-for-all death (Hebrews 9:26). Scripture nowhere inserts an artificial two-millennium gap.
2 Thessalonians 2:1–4: Paul explicitly warns believers not to be deceived: our gathering together unto Christ cannot happen until two visible signs occur: the apostasy and the revelation of the Man of Sin. A signless, secret rapture is refuted by the Apostle.
John 6:39–54 & 2 Thessalonians 1:6–10: The resurrection of the righteous is fixed to "the last day." The gathering of believers and the judgment of the ungodly are synchronized into a single, public event when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven in flaming fire.
Berean Verdict: Scripture teaches a singular Second Coming at the "last day," not a multi-stage secret return. Christ’s death fulfilled the redemptive mandates of Daniel 9 without an artificial parenthesis.
The Berean Systematic Examination
1. The Hermeneutic
Dispensational dogma insists on a uniform, flat literalism applied mechanically to all Old Testament prophecies, claiming that any non-literal application constitutes illegitimate spiritualization. When examined against apostolic Scripture (Colossians 2:16–17; Matthew 2:15; Hebrews 10:1), this hermeneutic is decisively refuted. The inspired New Testament writers operated by redemptive-historical typology, revealing that physical Old Covenant institutions, national events, and ceremonies were temporary shadows (skia) intentionally designed to find their true reality and ultimate substance (sōma) in the Person and work of Jesus Christ.
2. The People of God
Dispensationalism asserts that God maintains two eternally distinct peoples with separate programs and destinies: an earthly people (national Israel) and a heavenly people (the Church). Apostolic Scripture (Ephesians 2:14–16; Galatians 3:28–29; 1 Peter 2:9) refutes this division. At the Cross, Christ completely abolished the enmity and the middle wall of partition, taking both believing Jews and believing Gentiles to forge "one new man" reconciled to God in one single body.
3. The Seed of Abraham
The dispensational framework teaches that the covenant promises given to Abraham belong primarily to his biological, physical descendants through Jacob. Testing this against the written Word (Galatians 3:16, 29; Romans 9:6–8; Philippians 3:3) refutes the claim: Paul explicitly declares that the promises were spoken to Abraham and his singular Seed, which is Christ. Consequently, physical descent guarantees nothing; it is those who belong to Christ by faith who are legally, spiritually, and covenantally Abraham's true seed and heirs according to the promise.
4. The Olive Tree
Dispensational theology conceptualizes two separate tracks and distinct programs running in parallel for Israel and the Gentiles. Paul’s definitive agricultural analogy in Romans 11:16–24 directly refutes this dualism by presenting one single domestic Olive Tree rooted in the Abrahamic promise. Unbelieving natural branches are broken off due to unbelief, believing Gentile branches are grafted into that very same root, and repentant ethnic Jews are grafted back into their own original olive tree through faith in the Messiah.
5. The True Israel
Dispensational teachers frequently claim as a lexical absolute that the term "Israel" in the New Testament always and only denotes ethnic Jews. This assertion fails under direct scriptural cross-examination (Romans 9:6; Galatians 6:15–16; Romans 2:28–29). Paul explicitly states, "For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel," redefining covenantal identity from the inside out: true circumcision is inward and of the Spirit, and the true "Israel of God" consists of the new creation body of regenerate believers who have abandoned all confidence in the flesh.
6. The Genesis 12:3 Mandate
Dispensationalism interprets Genesis 12:3 ("I will bless them that bless thee...") as an enduring geopolitical mandate requiring unconditional foreign-policy alignment with modern secular or ethnic nations. The apostolic witness (Galatians 3:8–14; John 3:36; Psalm 2:11–12) refutes this application. Scripture defines the "blessing of Abraham" not as a worldly political treaty, but as justification by faith and the impartation of the Holy Spirit received exclusively through Jesus Christ, the singular Seed to whom all nations must bow.
7. The Land Promises
Dispensational dogma maintains that the territorial land grant from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates remains unfulfilled, requiring a future terrestrial realization for national Israel. This premise is contradicted both historically and covenantally by the written Word (Joshua 21:43–45; 1 Kings 4:21; Romans 4:13; Hebrews 11:13–16). Under Joshua and Solomon, Scripture records that not one word failed of all the good things God promised—all came to pass. Furthermore, the New Testament expands the temporal, localized type of Canaan into its ultimate antitype: Abraham being made the heir of the entire cosmos (kosmos), pointing to the New Heavens and the New Earth.
8. The Davidic Throne
Dispensationalism teaches that Christ is not presently seated upon the Throne of David, but is merely seated on the Father's throne in heaven awaiting a terrestrial reign in earthly Jerusalem. Apostolic preaching directly refutes this postponement (Acts 2:30–36; Hebrews 1:3; Revelation 3:21). On the Day of Pentecost, Peter explicitly cited David’s prophecy to declare that God raised Christ from the dead precisely to seat Him upon David's throne, exalting Him to the right hand of the Majesty on high as both Lord and Christ.
9. The Tabernacle of David
The dispensational system argues that the rebuilding of David's fallen tent (prophesied in Amos 9:11–12) refers to a future political restoration of the Davidic kingdom in a Jewish millennium. The Apostle James settles this at the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:13–18), authoritatively declaring that Amos 9 was being fulfilled in the first century through the resurrection of Christ and the gathering of Gentiles into the covenant community without circumcision.
10. The Kingdom of God
Dispensationalism asserts that because national Israel rejected Jesus, the Kingdom of God was officially withdrawn, suspended, and postponed to a future dispensation. The New Testament witness (Colossians 1:13; Matthew 12:28; Romans 14:17; Acts 28:31) refutes this premise. The Kingdom was inaugurated in power during the First Advent; believers are not waiting for an earthly political era to experience it, but have already been "translated into the kingdom of his dear Son."
11. The New Covenant
Dispensational theology restricts the direct covenantal ownership of Jeremiah 31:31 strictly to ethnic Israel and Judah, reducing the Church to secondary participants enjoying mere soteriological "overflow." Apostolic Scripture (Luke 22:20; 1 Corinthians 11:25; Hebrews 8:6–13; 2 Corinthians 3:3–6) refutes this division. Christ enacted the New Covenant in His blood, and the Holy Spirit explicitly applies Jeremiah's prophecy directly to individual regenerate believers—the spiritual ekklēsia—who are the actual ministers and participants of this covenant, having God's law written personally upon their minds and hearts.
12. The Way of Salvation
Classical dispensational structures draw such rigid divides between administrations that they create different conditions, probationary tests, or means of salvation across history (e.g., Law vs. Grace). Scripture thoroughly refutes this fragmentation (Genesis 15:6; Romans 4:1–8; Galatians 3:8; Acts 15:11). From the beginning, there has only ever been one gospel and one way of salvation: unmerited justification by grace alone through faith alone in the Messiah, with both Abraham before the Law and David under the Law saved through imputed righteousness.
13. Daniel’s 70th Week
Dispensational eschatology requires inserting an unmentioned 2,000-year hiatus between the 69th and 70th weeks of Daniel 9:24–27, assigning the final seven-year covenant to the future Antichrist. The biblical text refutes this artificial chasm. Daniel’s seventy weeks form a continuous unit fulfilled in Christ, who confirmed the New Covenant with the many (Matthew 26:28) and caused the necessity of Levitical sacrifices and oblations to permanently cease by His once-for-all sacrificial death on the cross (Hebrews 9:26; 10:8–10).
14. Temple and Animal Sacrifices
Dispensationalism anticipates a literal, rebuilt stone temple in Jerusalem where animal blood sacrifices will be reinstituted during a future millennium. This teaching stands in direct contradiction to the entire Epistle to the Hebrews (Hebrews 8:13; 10:11–18; 1 Corinthians 3:16). Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever and sat down. Because full remission of sin has been secured at Calvary, Scripture declares that "there is no more offering for sin"; returning to the blood of bulls and goats reverses redemptive history and diminishes the sufficiency of the cross.
15. The Second Coming
Dispensationalism divides the return of Christ into a two-stage eschatology: an imminent, signless, secret rapture of the Church, followed years later by a public physical revelation. The apostolic Scriptures (2 Thessalonians 2:1–4; John 6:39–54; 2 Thessalonians 1:7–10; Matthew 24:29–31) refute this bifurcation. The gathering of the saints and the resurrection of the just are explicitly synchronized with the judgment of the ungodly and the sound of the last trump, all occurring at a single, sign-preceded climax on "the last day."
The Synthesis
Dispensationalism requires reading the New Testament through the lens of an unfulfilled, physical Old Testament blueprint. The Berean, apostolic method does the exact opposite: the Apostles read the Old Testament through the finished work and cosmic supremacy of Jesus Christ (2 Corinthians 1:20; Ephesians 1:9–10).
In Christ, the shadows have met their substance, the dividing wall is abolished, the covenants are confirmed, and all believers—Jew and Gentile—stand together as the one, undivided household of God.

The Berean Call: Searching the Word and Submitting to His Will
A genuine Berean does not receive any doctrine, tradition, or system on the authority of men, seminaries, or reference notes, but searches the Scriptures daily to see whether these things are so (Acts 17:11). Theological systems constructed by human logic often divide what God has joined together and bind what God has set free. Let the seeker of truth take every proposition back to the living, inerrant Word of God, testing every spirit and every doctrine against the whole counsel of Scripture (1 Thessalonians 5:21; 1 John 4:1). Above all intellectual analysis, let every heart bow in complete submission to the Father, seeking not to conform the Word to human preference, but praying earnestly that His truth prevail, that Christ maintain the preeminence in all things, and that His sovereign will be done on earth as it is in heaven (Matthew 6:10; Colossians 1:18).

•Pakistan–India: May 2025 military escalation after a terror attack in Kashmir. A ceasefire followed. Trump claimed mediation via tariff threats. Pakistan thanked Trump and supported a Nobel nomination. Credit is disputed.

Trump was central to the negotiations. Long-term resolution of Gaza remains incomplete (disarmament, governance, reconstruction unresolved).

In short, there were real diplomatic efforts and some concrete results (notably Armenia-Azerbaijan and the Gaza hostages), but the “settled eight wars” framing is not accurate.

The United States sanctioned the ICC as an institution — not individual officials this time, the Court itself, placed on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals list under Executive Order 14203. Dollar clearing, banking rails, American technology dependencies: withdrawn. General License 13 authorizes specified wind-down transactions until 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 7, 2027; separate General Licenses 14, 15, and 16 address telecommunications and enterprise software, pensions, and detainee-related transactions, respectively. Salaries and routine operations needed for the wind-down are permitted only inside that license's scope and period — outside it, banking, insurance, procurement, and other business with the SDN-listed Court is prohibited. Marco Rubio's statement was undisguised: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC." Then the part that matters most, and that most coverage will underplay: "And we expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC, and that rely on American service members for their defense, to rein in this rogue court. If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, piece by piece, until Americans are threatened no longer." That is the alliance itself being invoked as the enforcement mechanism — the security umbrella is not separate from the sanctions, it is their second barrel. The 125 states parties are being told, in plain language, that the American defense guarantee and ICC membership are now in tension, and to choose. Hours earlier, the Nobel Committee awarded the Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, a former ICC judge — having pointedly passed over Trump, who has campaigned for the prize openly. The timing may be coincidence. It landed as message.

Akane's statement calls the sanctions "an attack against sovereign States that have created the Court" and "an assault on the rule of law," insists the Court acts "only on the basis of the law and the evidence," and warns that "the Court cannot stand alone — its fate now rests also in the hands of the states that created it."

Read that last sentence twice. It is the tell. A court claiming to stand above politics, declaring that its survival depends on political actors supplying resources and cover — that is not a refutation of the sanctions, it is a description of the dependency the sanctions exploit. The institution's claim to transcend politics is sustained entirely by politics. This is host-indexed autonomy under pressure: the Court runs on substrates — financial rails, software ecosystems, personnel mobility, state cooperation — controlled by the very parties it claims jurisdiction over without their consent.

The deeper collision is structural. The Rome Statute's 125 parties are the constitutive source the Court invokes. But the sanctions respond to the Court exercising authority over non-parties — the United States and Israel — whose consent was never given. The actual jurisdictional mechanism deserves examination rather than a slogan. Under Article 12(2)(a), the Court can claim jurisdiction over crimes allegedly committed on the territory of a state party even when the accused is a national of a non-party. That is the territorial-jurisdiction theory, and its logic is not exotic: states routinely exercise criminal jurisdiction over foreign nationals for conduct on their territory. But the theory requires a territorial predicate capable of carrying the authority being asserted. In the Israeli proceedings, that predicate is Palestine — and now the conversation becomes considerably more interesting.

The so-called State of Palestine was proclaimed by the Palestine Liberation Organization in Algiers on November 15, 1988. A proclamation by the PLO is not, to my mind, the creation of a sovereign country. I have no interest in a roll call of governments that subsequently recognized it, or in being instructed to treat diplomatic recognition as though it materialized a functioning state. The PLO can declare whatever it likes. Recognition can confer legal standing, and Palestine did acquire UN non-member observer-state status in 2012 before acceding to the Rome Statute in 2015; those are facts about the international institutional record, not proof of an independent Palestinian government exercising effective control over a settled territory with the capabilities of a sovereign state. A diplomatic fiction may be adequate for the diplomacy that created it. That does not oblige me to mistake it for the material thing. In this dispute, Palestine is a contested statehood claim being used as a load-bearing jurisdictional foundation against a country that never joined the ICC. I am profoundly skeptical of the legitimacy of that construction, and I do not owe the PLO's declaration an ounce of reverence.

Here is the extraordinary maneuver: the ICC did not settle the statehood question it needed the territory to carry. In its February 5, 2021 ruling, the majority said it was not constitutionally competent to decide Palestine's statehood for the international community or settle its borders. It nevertheless treated Palestine's accepted accession as sufficient to make it a state party for the purposes of the Rome Statute, extending the Court's claimed territorial jurisdiction to Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The legal distinction is real: a state party's territory can ordinarily supply jurisdiction over a non-party's nationals under Article 12, and the ICC's ruling supplies its treaty-law basis for treating Palestine that way. My objection is to the political and juridical sleight of hand embedded in the premise. The Court admits it is not settling whether this is a state in the full international sense, then proceeds to make that disputed entity's treaty status the gateway to asserting criminal power over Israeli officials. It can call Palestine a state for its own statutory purposes. It cannot make that classification synonymous with effective sovereignty simply by pronouncing it from The Hague.

Even indulging that entire theory for the sake of argument, what exactly can this Court do with it? On November 21, 2024, the ICC issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant; in April 2025, its Appeals Chamber returned an Israeli jurisdictional challenge for further consideration. It can issue warrants, circulate demands, stage press conferences, and make travel diplomatically complicated. It cannot send its own police into Israel, seize Israeli officials, and drag them to The Hague. The ICC itself acknowledges that arrests and surrender require cooperating states. A warrant may have real effects where a sovereign chooses to execute it, but the decisive force belongs to that sovereign, not the ICC. The Court has a signature, a seal, and a theory. It does not have the independent coercive capacity to make Israel obey. That is the reality behind the performance, and no recital of international recognition changes it.

The whole structure is a cascade of borrowed capacities. The PLO proclaimed a state whose sovereignty remains profoundly contested; the ICC treated that state's treaty accession as a sufficient territorial jurisdictional predicate; the resulting warrants depend on still other states volunteering their police, airports, courts, and borders to enforce them. Each stage presents a legal or diplomatic designation as if it carried power inherently, while the actual power resides somewhere else. This is not an argument that the Court's legal acts have no consequences. It is an argument about who actually possesses the means to produce those consequences, and who is borrowing prestige and enforcement from the institutions and states around them. Treaty-delegated jurisdictional performance has now collided with non-consenting sovereign capacity. Akane invokes the states that created the Court as the wellspring of legitimacy. Washington is demonstrating that the states sustaining the world's financial and security infrastructure may have a very different answer about whose commands prevail.

The operational record does not rescue the "only law and evidence" claim. Afghanistan investigations that risked American personnel were deprioritized; the warrants against Israeli leadership proceeded. I will not litigate the underlying allegations here — that is someone else's argument, and I am sidestepping it deliberately. The point is structural, not substantive: a court that activates selectively is not doing law, it is doing politics in legal costume. The Hague complex functions as a legitimacy foundry, converting narrative preferences into the aesthetic of law and then exporting the aesthetic as binding norm.

So those words. They do not debate the Court's self-description; they decline the framing in which the Court's games are the only games being played. One side optimizes for narrative capture and the conversion of institutional prestige into constraint on enforcement-capable actors. The other optimizes for non-subsumption of core security functions and the chokepoints — financial, technological — that make enforcement possible at all.

Everyone involved understands the shape of this now. The annoyance is tedious and we've run out of patience. Few things could bring me as much joy as seeing the ICC get their metaphorical teeth kicked in. It is a deep delight to the blood to watch an institution that mistook prestige for power discover the difference. The Court has been offered the same choice for years: end the threats, or be ended. It chose, again, to perform. And let us be precise about what has already happened. We did not threaten sanctions — we deployed them. The Court is on the SDN list, the designations are in force, and the financial exclusion is operating as I write this. What the ICC has is six months of wind-down: six months to avoid even rougher waters. End the threats, or be ended — the choice was issued, and the clock is already running. We are dismantling the institution, piece by piece — through sanctions already deployed, financial exclusion already in motion, technological denial, diplomatic pressure, and the withdrawal of every dependency we have the power to withdraw. This is no longer a dispute about whether we respect its pretensions. It is a question of whether the Court can survive the consequences of continuing to impose them on us. So now we play the game it wanted to play — the one where jurisdiction is not a declaration but a capacity. Performances end when the funding does.

🇪🇺 🇷🇺 Europe breaks with Trump on Russian diesel: Kallas says Brussels will not ease pressure and foreign ministers move Monday on the largest Russia sanctions listings of the war

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas answered the US diesel deal on Saturday with a refusal to follow. "Suspending sanctions on Russian diesel provides Moscow with more revenue to wage war," she wrote on X. "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't." She said EU foreign ministers are set to approve on Monday the biggest set of sanctions listings aimed at Russia's war machine since the invasion began, and cited more than 80 Ukrainian civilians killed over two days. She also said Russia has stepped up hybrid attacks on EU states and NATO allies.

The package itself was settled before the diesel announcement. Agence Europe reported on October 7 that EU ambassadors approved listings of 743 individuals and 826 entities tied to Russia's military-industrial complex, plus 77 entries linked to the recent Duma elections, including three members of the electoral commission. Formal adoption is due Monday in Luxembourg. By Agence Europe's count, nearly 4,500 people and entities would then be under EU sanctions for the war. What is new is the political setting. The vote now lands as a public contrast with Washington, which on Friday issued a temporary license for Russian diesel exports.

London and Berlin lined up with Kyiv. A Downing Street spokesperson said Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke to Zelensky, offered "complete solidarity," and that the two agreed Russia should accept "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end attacks on Black Sea shipping, per the BBC. Germany said it will keep pursuing new EU sanctions on Russia, and a European Commission spokesperson told RFE/RL the bloc will keep cutting its dependence on Russian fossil fuels. Zelensky said he spoke to Emmanuel Macron about air defense, warning of more missile strikes in the coming days, and to Finland's Alexander Stubb, with ammunition for the F-16s that intercept Shahed drones due in coming days.

The split is a sign that the allies Washington asked to tighten the screws will not follow it into loosening them, even as US diesel hits $6.28 a gallon per AAA. For Europeans, the test comes Monday and then at the October 15 and 16 summit. A listing is not a cash measure, and Washington's license does not bind the EU. The open question is whether Brussels can keep pressure on Russian revenue while a US waiver lets Russian diesel reach the global market.

text:
When Elon Musk and the other AI oligarchs tell you that the future is wonderful and AI is gonna bring Universal High Income, let’s be clear: that’s a complete and total load of horseshit. 

And they know it. 

So, why are they saying it? 

Because they are hoping you won’t run for the guillotines yet. They are trying to pacify us with promises that are neither economically nor politically credible under the system we actually have. This is straight-up gaslighting, and I’m incredibly annoyed that the media is letting them get away with it.

I’ve heard this income fantasy over and over again. And yes, sometimes they get asked how it’s supposed to work. They talk about “dividends,” about everyone sharing in the enormous wealth AI will create. 

Apparently that counts as an answer, because the obvious follow-up never seems to come.

How do you get THAT through our political system?

We are over $40 trillion in debt. The federal minimum wage is still $7.25 an hour. We are cutting healthcare and food assistance for people who are already struggling. We can’t agree to adequately fund the safety net we have, but somehow we’re going to completely transform our economic system and shower wealth on the entire population?

Apparently all we need to do is eliminate their jobs first. Then everyone in Washington will become very concerned about their quality of life.

I’m not arguing that AI can’t produce enormous wealth. 

I’m asking what country these people think we live in. 

Because in the United States, getting help to people who need it is a political fight every single time. 

Suddenly calling it a “dividend” doesn’t make that go away.

Under a different system, perhaps this could happen. China can make decisions about the direction of its economy by edict in ways our government cannot. 

That doesn’t mean it would choose to share the wealth fairly. But at least there’s a conceivable way to make that decision. Here, we’re supposed to believe that the same political system currently cutting assistance is going to agree to distribute the profits of privately owned AI companies to everybody.

Fine. Explain how. Explain what changes, who makes it happen, and why we should believe any of it while watching the exact opposite happen in front of us.

And let’s say, somehow, we actually get this “high income.” Where does that leave the people who own the technology? Trillionaires by the dozen? We get an allowance and they get a level of wealth and power that makes today’s billionaires look middle class?

Who’s giving us this money, anyway? What happens if they decide we don’t deserve it anymore?

If you’ve eliminated my ability to earn a living, and I depend on a payment somebody else can reduce or take away, that somebody has control over my life. I don’t particularly care how nice the allowance is. What am I allowed to refuse? What happens if I object to the terms? Where do I go?

These are fairly important details to leave out of your wonderful future.

Then there’s the assumption that we should all be thrilled because we won’t have to work. As though the only thing anyone ever got out of working was a paycheck.

A physicist or mathematician who dedicated their life to developing their mind wasn’t just killing time until somebody offered them free money. And as a software engineer, I can appreciate what AI lets me do while also understanding what it means to see the economic value of decades spent learning to code, debug and solve problems get stripped away. Those aren’t contradictory feelings. I can love the tool and still have a problem with where this is going.

People already struggle in retirement because they lose the structure and purpose their work gave them. Even people with plenty of money. What, are we all supposed to jet ski all day, every day, and that’s gonna make up for it?

We already know retirement can be a difficult adjustment. Some people find new interests and give themselves something to work toward. Others spend years feeling lost. Having all the free time in the world doesn’t help much when you don’t know what to do with yourself or feel that anything you do matters. People can become depressed, withdraw, or turn to alcohol and drugs to fill the hours. Why are we talking about imposing this on entire generations as though everyone will naturally find their way?

I’m retired. I know perfectly well that you can find meaning outside a job. I also know there’s a difference between choosing how to spend your life and having your choices taken away while somebody tells you how lucky you are.

You don’t get to take away people’s livelihoods, make their expertise disposable, put them on an allowance, and then act confused when they aren’t grateful. People want to do things that matter. They want some say in their own lives. “You’ll still be able to buy stuff” is an insult dressed up as reassurance.

What bothers me is how much of this we’re being asked to accept on faith. The companies get to accumulate the ownership and power now. The rest of us are supposed to trust that some future government will arrange for us to share in it, despite what our government is actually doing today.

These men understand money. They understand ownership. They know that producing wealth and agreeing to share it are entirely different things. Yet they keep presenting the second as though it automatically follows from the first, and the people interviewing them keep letting it slide.

That’s why I call it a lie. They are selling a political fantasy as a technological certainty because it makes what they’re doing sound good for everybody.

Before you tell me again about my wonderful future, explain who pays me, what rights I have, and how any of this survives contact with American politics.

Until then, stop telling me how grateful I’m going to be.

text:
The 4 BEST signals for outbound marketing:

(after sending over 50,000,000+ cold emails)

All of these are broad enough for anyone to use:

1) Job postings. If they're hiring for the role that owns what you sell, that's your why now. Mention the posting in your first line, and the prospect knows exactly why you're writing this week.

2) Watch for a tool swap in their stack. Name the tool they just moved off, right at the top of the email. Builtwith if its website tech, job post descriptions for complex migrations, handraiser emails for everything else.

3) Scrape their reviews, website and ads to find something commentworthy and relevant to your offer. Connect it with your offer and pitch. Short simple punchy.

4) Look for someone new in the seat you sell to. Don’t state the obvious and say “saw you just joined”. Just reach them while they're still new and make them a good offer.

Most senders get “why me” and “why you” right without much effort. Then comes the ask for a call, and NOTHING in the email explains “why now”

A prospect can agree with every line you wrote and still not reply if nothing tells them why it has to be NOW.

Brother Sisay,

Let me take your own rule seriously, because it is a good one: arguments stand or fall on their merits, not their authors' motives. On that basis, I accept your correction. The line was Zemene's, quoted in context, and it should not have been read as a confession. So let us return to the merits.

The same discipline cuts both ways. "Explain its terms" is a fair demand, but it is not an argument. And after several days, Dawit's question still stands unanswered: what is the alternative, and how does it better protect Amhara lives? You asked for the case. Here it is, built on the record rather than on sentiment.

I. What absence has cost us: 1991–92. The Amhara entered the post-Derg order without an organized political-military force of their own. The record of what followed is not rhetoric. In June 1992, members of the All-Amhara People's Organization could not even register candidates in many constituencies. Amnesty International reported that OLF members allegedly killed dozens of Amhara in early 1992. In Bedeno, in eastern Ethiopia, more than 150 people were killed in April 1992; 280 people were later charged with genocide. The Moresh study records that at Arba Gugu at least 500 Amhara were thrown alive from the cliff of Mosa Giyorgis.

This is the Hararghe and Arsi that Dawit grew up in. Those communities were not destroyed because they chose the wrong allies. They were destroyed because they had no organization, no army and no seat. The constitution that followed was written without them, and every grievance since, from Wollega to Metekel, flows from that founding absence.

II. What loyalty has cost us: Pretoria. Some argue Amhara is safest by standing alone, or by trusting the state. We tested that too. Amhara forces fought beside the federal army in 2020–2022. Yet when Addis Ababa and the TPLF met in Pretoria, Amhara representatives were not at the table. The accord left the contested territories and the return of the displaced unresolved. Within months, the government moved to dissolve the regional forces that had fought for it, and the present war began. Alliance with the state bought Amhara no seat. It bought disarmament.

III. What the present costs us. Dawit's claim that this government is the gravest threat in living memory is not hyperbole. The state-appointed Ethiopian Human Rights Commission confirmed that government forces extrajudicially killed at least 45 civilians in Merawi in January 2024. Human Rights Watch reported summary executions there. In April 2025, a drone strike on Gedeb in East Gojjam killed over 100 people; eyewitnesses said they were civilians building a school fence. ACLED had by then recorded 73 air and drone strikes in Amhara. A government that says drone strikes will continue whenever targets are found is not a negotiating partner waiting to be persuaded.

IV. What the alliance offers. The framework is thin by design: a transitional government bound by a charter, an end to the wars, protection of rights, and a national dialogue. You treat that thinness as a defect. I treat it as the opening. Ethiopia's next order has not been written, and for the first time since 1991, Amhara will hold a pen.

The benefits are concrete. Strategically, a state fighting on three fronts cannot concentrate its drones and divisions on Gojjam and Gondar; dispersal is measured in villages spared. Protectively, the Amhara most exposed today live in Wollega, Metekel and the periphery, and a channel to the armed actors there is the only lever short of total victory. Politically, a recognized party to the transition cannot be dismissed as bandits or a proxy, and recognition is the precondition for every guarantee you demand.

That’s an oversimplification. Yes, Hamas’s ideology has included rejecting Israel’s legitimacy, and that absolutely deserves criticism. But saying Palestinians have simply been offered a state ‘over and over’ and irrationally said no leaves out the actual terms, borders, settlements, Jerusalem, refugees, security arrangements, and the fact that some proposals were never formally accepted or finalized. Camp David in 2000 ended without an agreement, Taba in 2001 also ended without a deal, and the 2008 negotiations continued until they collapsed rather than producing a simple Palestinian ‘no.’
And Hamas isn't synonymous with every Palestinian—Hamas itself accepted a Palestinian state along the 1967 borders in its 2017 political document, while still refusing to recognize Israel.
You can condemn Hamas's ideology and attacks without pretending the entire conflict is simply ‘Israel offered peace, Palestinians refused, therefore keep fighting.’ That isn't an accurate description of the history

V. The hard part, said plainly. I know the OLA's record. In June 2022, at least 230 Amhara were killed in western Oromia in a massacre attributed to the OLA, which it denies. I know the TPLF's record, from 1991 to Chenna and Kobo. So do you. But that history is precisely why Amhara must negotiate as an armed equal, not wait to be represented by others. Pretoria proves that settlements are made by those at the table. The TPLF has now dismantled Pretoria's architecture, and Western Tigray will be decided again. Outside the coalition, it is decided between Addis Ababa and Mekelle. Inside it, it cannot be decided without AFNM's consent. Alliance does not surrender the question. Isolation surrenders the seat.

VI. On the leadership. You ask who compromises what, on whose authority. The answer is an organization that, in January, did what Fano had failed to do for three years: it united Gojjam, Gondar, Wollo, Shewa and Eskinder's faction under one command. You may doubt its chairman. But the authority to negotiate for a movement belongs to those who carry it at the front, not to its observers, however learned or long-serving. Our task in the diaspora is to hold that leadership to account against outcomes, not to veto its strategy in advance.

VII. A proposal worthy of your standards. Let us agree on the benchmarks by which this alliance should be judged within six to twelve months:

1Measurable protection of Amhara civilians in Oromia and Benishangul.
2Amhara representation written into any transitional charter.
3No settlement of Western Tigray, Raya or Wolkait without AFNM's consent.
4AFNM's command autonomy preserved.
5No separate peace: no member settles with Addis Ababa alone, as the TPLF did at Pretoria.

If it fails those tests, I will say so publicly, beside you. In return, set out your alternative in equal detail. Criticism that never names an alternative is not scrutiny. It is the luxury of never being wrong.
In 1992, the Amhara of Bedeno and Arba Gugu had critics enough. What they lacked was a seat and an army. The house is burning. Not every firefighter is competent, but listing their faults from the street has never put out a flame.

Match Analysis: Arsenal vs Leeds | #AFC 

Consistent patterns I noticed today.

1. High Regains, Verticality and Attacking Transitions

One thing I enjoyed was our willingness to progress vertically and attack immediately after regaining possession. Compared to Brighton, we clearly adapted our approach, increasing tempo and looking to bypass Leeds' aggressive press, whether through quick combinations, direct balls over the top or immediate line-breaking progression.

Our high regains were particularly encouraging, allowing us to attack retreating defensive lines before Leeds could reorganise. It was a clear weakness in Leeds' system as I alluded to in my pre-match analysis. Madueke was a clear outlet alongside Havertz and Gyokeres, with his pace proving particularly effective in exploiting space in behind and delivering dangerous, varied balls into the box. However, there were recurring issues with decision-making and the execution of the first pass following regains, particularly surrounding Odegaard, Rice and MLS. At times, we dwelled in possession rather than immediately progressing, allowing Leeds to recover, challenge and reset (Especially in the first half).

Raya's direct distribution was also effective, particularly when finding Havertz to initiate transitions and using second ball chasers or runners in behind.

Nevertheless, I really enjoyed the tactical adaptation and our intent to attack quickly rather than settle into slower circulation.

2. The Impact of Noni Madueke and Holding Width

We saw a clear difference in our attacking structure, particularly in final-third progression and box entries. Madueke was excellent, recording 9 box entries (@kashONdaCounter), 4 key passes, 2/2 successful dribbles and an incredible 11 of his 27 carries were progressive, with 168.1m in total progression.

What I particularly enjoyed was how consistently he was allowed to repeat his actions. I feel that repetition will be crucial in helping him develop consistency in a relatively unfamiliar position.

His width was a constant feature, allowing him to repeatedly isolate Bogle before driving inside or delivering dangerous crosses. His relationship with Calafiori was especially encouraging, with the Italian's underlapping movements exploiting the LHS created by Noni's positioning. I particularly enjoyed seeing Noni hold maximum width before accelerating at a retreating Bogle.

He also offered a clear (and our primary) outlet in transition, consistently looking to run in behind and exploit Leeds' high defensive line. There appeared to be a trade-off in his defensive responsibilities to maximise this threat (didn't track for Leeds' goal), although his recovery runs were encouraging at times. His body manipulation when dribbling was another positive, allowing him to create separation and attack defenders more effectively.

There are still limitations with his weaker foot (despite his fantastic cross), but for his first game on the left wing in a year, I came away very impressed.

3. Dealing with Wide Threats

Dealing with wide threats was an area I thought we struggled with today. Leeds repeatedly created dangerous situations through wide areas, with Bogle especially threatening both with his deliveries and attacking alongside DCL. I'd rather give credit to Leeds than overly criticise Konsa and Gabriel, although I do feel they could have done better in certain situations, specifically the goal where Konsa jumps out.

There was a clear attacking emphasis down our left, with Noni acting as the primary outlet in transition. This occasionally came at the expense of our defensive coverage, with Noni's failure to track his man particularly evident for the goal with Justin bombing forward from wide CB.

Leeds' back post runs were also dangerous, as we struggled to track runners and defend deliveries into the box. On a few occasions, they managed to find a free man at the back post, exposing weaknesses in our defensive organisation.

4. The Clear Impact of Bruno Guimaraes and Viktor Gyokeres

Bruno's introduction brought a level of directness through central areas that we'd been missing, especially before the second goal. His willingness to carry forward, break lines and occupy advanced spaces offered considerably more verticality than MLS and I believe the substitution was fantastically timed. For me, these are exactly the in possession qualities we signed him for, alongside his brilliantly taken goal with a fantastic ability to set himself for the strike.

Gyokeres was encouraging too IMO. His first touch and hold up play looked much improved, while his physical presence and consistent channel runs helped stretch Leeds' back line and open space for wide players to receive under minimal pressure. His decision-making when Trafford came out was frustrating, as it was a genuine goalscoring opportunity.

Other Notes:
Hincapie was excellent with his overlapping movements, showing a nuance with Noni drifting centrally. Timber was solid throughout, occasionally showing good attacking intent as well. Merino was brilliant in the final chance with his flick on to Gyokeres before Saka missed the chance.

Other Patterns:

Cutbacks from high regains against retreating defences kept creating the best chances, with Odegaard as the spare man/late runner again. Same theme as previous games.

This game was built for direct play, not the calm, patient circulation we're used to and we adapted well. Once Bruno and Gyokeres came on, Leeds' back line dropped a few yards deeper and the channel runs continued.

Leeds' press was aggressive throughout, with strong challenges from Tanaka, Ampadu and Stach. I thought Tanaka was fantastic in the first 60 minutes. Felt like he was absolutely everywhere.

text:
Actor James Earl Jones gets some instruction (on pugilism, not acting) from trainer Mushy Callahan, during filming of 'The Great White Hope', which was released on October 11, 1970.

The film was directed by Martin Ritt, starring James Earl Jones, Jane Alexander, Chester Morris, Hal Holbrook, Beah Richards and Moses Gunn. Jones and Alexander, who also appeared in the same roles in the stage versions, received Best Actor and Actress Academy Award nominations for their performances.

The film and play is based on the true story of boxer Jack Johnson and his first wife, Etta Terry Duryea, and the controversy over their marriage and Duryea's death by suicide in 1912.

Set between 1910 and 1915, the story follows Jack Jefferson, patterned after real-life boxer Jack Johnson, going on a hot streak of victories in the boxing ring as he defeats every white boxer around. Soon the press and others who want to see white people win at sports, announce the search for a "great white hope", a white boxer who will defeat Jefferson for the heavyweight title.

Jefferson, meanwhile, prepares for a few more matches, but he lets his guard down by courting the beautiful, and white, Eleanor Bachman, and when everyone, including Jack's black "wife", discover this, the tensions grow to fever pitch. Jack's close black friends become scared over his pushing the envelope of success and the white authorities conspire to frame him for unlawful sexual relations with Eleanor and thereby take away his title. It leads to jealousy, a run from the law, and finally, tragedy.
----------------------------------------------------------
Among the actors Mushy Callahan trained for films were Montgomery Clift (From Here to Eternity), James Dean (Rebel Without a Cause), Kirk Douglas (Champion), Errol Flynn (Gentleman Jim), James Earl Jones (The Great White Hope), Burt Lancaster (Jim Thorpe – All-American), Anthony Quinn (Requiem for a Heavyweight), and Elvis Presley (Kid Galahad).

Mushy Callahan, born Vincent Morris Scheer in New York City, held the (NBA) World  Junior Welterweight Championship from September of 1926 to February of 1930.

Recognition at time is disputed. The Wisconsin commission recognized Pinky Mitchell while others recognized James Herring and even others recognized the title vacant or not at all.

Callahan acted in, and served as a boxing technical assistant on a number of boxing movies. He trained Elvis Presley for his role in Kid Galahad and also portrayed the referee in the movie's final climatic bout.

Callahan finished his career at 49-15-3 with 22 KO wins.

He was inducted into the World Boxing Hall of Fame posthumously in 1989.

From The Jewish Boxing Blog:

Mushy Callahan held the junior welterweight world championship for nearly three and a half years and after his boxing career ended, he trained the biggest Hollywood stars on the sets of their movies. Yet among fans of Jewish boxing, Callahan isn't revered like Benny Leonard nor is he admired like Barney Ross. 
Though his championship reign was long, it was hampered by several factors: the "synthetic" nature of his crown, his losses in over-the-weight bouts, and his propensity to duck the toughest challengers. His conversion to Catholicism after his career also contributed to Callahan's fallen star within the Jewish boxing community.
Vincent Morris Scheer was born on November 3, 1904 in New York to Jewish Austrian parents named Max and Anna. The family moved across the country to Los Angeles and settled in Boyle Heights when Vincent, who was known as Moishele, was two years old. Max sold produce near the intersection of Brooklyn Ave and Soto. Meanwhile, young Moishele got into a lot of fights. He resented when other kids called him "Maurice" and had no problem showing them with his fists. After a while, no one wanted to call him Maurice anymore, so he soon developed the nickname of Mushy, which would stick for the rest of his life. As a youngster, he worked as a newsboy, a profession that required boys to fight each other for access to the best corners.
At the age of ten, Scheer joined the Main Street Gym, which was also known as the Newsboys' Club. He fought in a lot of smokers and took the surname Callahan from a local fight promoter. His childhood friend, future Olympic gold medalist and two-time world champion Jackie Fields, remembered, "Mushy Callahan was the greatest. We were raised together selling papers. But he was always the big shot."
Once evening, Fields wanted Mushy to get him tickets to a show at the Orpheum. "When I asked him to get me two tickets he said, 'Get in line, you punk you.' So we almost had a fight on the street," Fields said.
Callahan turned pro in 1923 and quickly became a hot prospect. The next year, he dropped a couple of decisions to Johnny Adams, a very popular fighter in Los Angeles who was good, but not great. Callahan didn't hit many other bumps in the road on his climb to the top, though. He beat a quality veteran in Red Herring, took two ten-round decisions from former lightweight world champion Jimmy Goodrich, and went 1-0-1 against a world class opponent named Ace Hudkins.
(Me: We have discussed Hudkins here a few times. he was quite the interesting character himself!)
The first fight against Hudkins, which took place on September 16, 1925, was one of the most exciting battles in L.A. that year. Most observers felt referee Larry McGrath's decision to call it a draw was fair, but Callahan and his team vehemently disagreed. Willie Goldstein, who worked Callahan's corner, climbed through the ropes and attacked McGrath, receiving a hard left hook from the ref in return. Callahan and his manager E.W. Sears were both fined and suspended until December. McGrath was also suspended. Goldstein was banned for life.
Callahan won the rematch and then took the two fights against Goodrich. He was extremely popular among fight fans in Los Angeles. His July 5, 1926 fight against Jack Silver, a fan favorite from San Francisco, was billed as a clash between Southern California and Northern California. Coincidentally, Silver, like Callahan, was a Jewish fighter who would convert to Catholicism, work in Hollywood after his boxing career was done, and have a long and distinguished career as a referee.
In one of the biggest fights in California since bouts of over four rounds were legalized at the start of 1925, Silver dominated Mushy over ten rounds. 
A month later Callahan lost to another good fighter, Baby Joe Gans. 
Despite, or maybe because of, the two losses, Callahan got a shot at junior welterweight champion, Pinky Mitchell. 
"Mitchell figured I was washed up," Callahan said years later. 
Mushy destroyed Mitchell, nearly knocking him out in then tenth and final round. "Everything I did was perfect," Callahan said. "One of those perfect fights."
Mitchell had held the title since its inception in 1923. 
Purists saw it as a "synthetic" title, a worrying addition to the traditional eight weight classes. In fact, the belt would basically become abandoned from 1935 until 1959.
After a few wins in non-title bouts, Callahan dropped a decision to Spug Myers. Though Myers was over the weight limit, Callahan was 140 pounds, so today he would have vacated his belt after the loss. He next fought undefeated beast Andy DiVodi at Madison Square Garden with the title on the line. "My biggest thrill came when I fought Andy DiVodi," Mushy said. "The New York papers were full of DiVodi, a big favorite, who was undefeated... I knocked him out in the second round."
Callahan was a wild-swinging fighter. 
"He had a funny way of throwing a one-two," Jackie Fields recalled. 
Mushy wasn't known as a knockout puncher, which made the win against DiVodi all the more impressive.
 He then avenged his loss to Spug Myers in his second title defense. A year after the loss to Silver, Callahan appeared to be a fighting champion who would risk his title against the best. He'd soon prove otherwise.
On July 12, 1927, at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Sammy Baker wrecked Callahan, punishing the champ's body to win by ninth round TKO. Both men were over 140, so Callahan remained champ. A loss to Dick Hoppe, a decent local fighter, made Mushy look like a paper champion. His manager claimed he was sick for the Hoppe fight.
His old friend Jackie Fields offered $25,000 if Callahan would risk his junior welterweight championship. Callahan refused, so they fought for the unofficial title of Jewish champion of Boyle Heights. 
"I kicked the hell out of him," Fields said. "That was the first time I ever bet on myself. I bet five hundred dollars on myself and we won it. He never spoke to me for years afterward. That was a great win because of being in the neighborhood and around our friends."
Still champ, Callahan had now lost three fights in a row. 
Boxing experts didn't even rate the champion as the #1 junior welterweight in their rankings, which was highly unusual. 
He avenged his loss to Hoppe and beat a couple of other mediocre fighters before losing some more. 
Callahan was 2-5-1 in his last eight fights, making zero title defenses in that span. Two years after his last defense, he finally put the title up against Fred Mahan. A deaf-mute, Mahan was more inspirational than great. Mushy stopped him in the third round.
Callahan lost to Goodrich before losing to Jack "Kid" Berg. On February 18, 1930, Callahan finally agreed to defend his title against a real contender when he faced Berg at Royal Albert Hall in London, this time with the title at stake. Joe Jacobs promised Mushy $10,000 for the fight. "He said I'd get ten thousand," Callahan lamented. "I never got ten thousand. When I got paid off, I only got five thousand." Jacobs, the promoter for Callahan-Berg II, was the manager of Max Schmeling.
"Over there I saw the handwriting on the wall," Mushy confided. "I couldn't possibly win the fight. He butted me in the eye and my eye started to puff up." It eventually closed and Callahan requested the referee to stop the fight in the tenth. As champ his middling record was 16-10-1, putting his title up for grabs just four times in nearly three and half years.
After two years off, Callahan fought thrice more. His final record was 49-16-3 with 22 KOs.
After his fighting career was over, Callahan began training Hollywood stars on the art of pugilism to prepare them for roles in boxing films. He worked with Elvis Presley, James Earl Jones, Kirk Douglas, and Errol Flynn, just to name a few. In the movie Gentleman Jim, Callahan served as a body double for Flynn in the fighting scenes. He worked as a referee at a high level in the Los Angeles area for nearly thirty years. He was a boxing judge for nearly twenty.
In 1934, he married Lilian Hill and converted to Catholicism.
Jews have been described as a race, a religion, a people, a tribe, and a nation, but the best way to describe us is a large family. We may argue, disagree, fight amongst ourselves, just as any family might, but we feel an indelible connection with one another. When someone chooses to leave our family, many of us take it hard. Fair or not, it's feels like a personal affront. While Benny Leonard and  Barney Ross stood up for Jews, Callahan, whose son would become a priest, left our family.
On June 14, 1986, world champion and Hollywood star Mushy Callahan passed away at the age of 80.

Mathematician Who Waited 50 Years for Proper Credit for Her Work Has Died

Listen · 8:21 min
10OCT2026, 
By Ama Sarpomaa
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/zMN2WzX4OX

At the Los Alamos National Laboratory, Mary Tsingou Menzel’s computer programming helped set the stage for chaos theory and other fields.

Mary Tsingou Menzel as a young mathematician. She joined what was then Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory in https://t.co/3M4ClLizLG...Los Alamos National Laboratory

Mary Tsingou arrived at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory in 1952, seven years after the testing facility in New Mexico helped propel the world into an age of nuclear proliferation. She was a recent college graduate with a mathematics degree and joined the cohort — almost all women — of “human computers.”

As Los Alamos continued to serve as a leader in Cold War scientific research, Ms. Tsingou was disappointed that her first task was to input simple math equations on a calculator. “It was pretty boring sitting there doing addition and subtraction,” she recalled in 2020 to a publication of the federal research lab.

But Ms. Tsingou was soon given the opportunity to work as an early programmer of MANIAC I, the lab’s first fully electronic computer. Her coding work — translating equations into the MANIAC-approved language of holes punched on tape — led to the creation in 1955 of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam (FPU) problem, named after the men who worked on the numerical experiment.

When the report was published, Ms. Tsingou was not listed as an author. Instead, her name was placed in a footnote: “We thank Miss Mary Tsingou for efficient coding of the problems and for running the computations on the Los Alamos MANIAC machine.”

“They didn’t know anything about programming,” she told The Los Alamos publication. “They set up the equations, and I did all the programming.”

The groundbreaking computational physics experiment observed surprising physical behaviors that propelled the development of nonlinear science, one of whose branches is chaos theory — an influential way of thinking about how subtle changes to the initial state of a complex system can eventually lead to wildly unpredictable outcomes. It offered scientists a new way of exploring the physical world, by showing, for the first time, the power of the computer to investigate phenomena too complex to visualize by hand or with traditional experiments.

Ms. Tsingou (later Menzel), who spent her nearly 40-year career as a programmer at what became Los Alamos National Laboratory, died on Aug. 27 at her home in Los Alamos. She was 97. Her death was confirmed by her daughter Ann Menzel.

The original MANIAC — an acronym for “Mathematical Analyzer, Numerical Integrator and Computer” — was seven feet high, nine feet wide, weighed 1,000 pounds and was fitted with about 3,000 vacuum tubes. It could make upward of 10,000 calculations per second, dramatically superior to computing by hand.

Through a series of trials, Ms. Tsingou and her fellow operators became so familiar with the computer that they could identify and address issues with code by ear. But the technology was so new that they were forced to “invent their way out of problems,” said Nicholas Lewis, a lab historian at Los Alamos.

“You had to use what the machine recognized, which was only ones and zeros,” Ms. Tsingou said of the laborious task of programming the MANIAC. “We typed the directions on a tape and put it in the machine.”

Her first exercise while learning to work with the hums and blinks of the primitive computer was to find the sine of an angle. After poring over her work for some time — computing, coding, checking and rechecking — she finally punched the tape.

“It worked immediately!” she said in a 2002 oral history interview with the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers.

She was invited to program an experiment for the mathematician Stanislaw Ulam and the physicists John Pasta and Enrico Fermi as they brainstormed ways to use the MANIAC to explore theories they couldn’t easily compute by hand.

They decided to observe the computationally simulated motion of a line of particles connected by springs, similar to a vibrating string. Their expectation was simple: When prompted, springs would cause energy to be shared throughout the entire system, resulting in random movement patterns.

But when Ms. Tsingou plotted the data she pulled from the MANIAC on to charts and graphs, the system appeared to vibrate in structured ways, periodically returning to its initial configuration. This revealed, numerically, that there can be hidden patterns in the motion of dynamically rich, or “nonlinear,” systems.

The revelation from the FPU problem strongly influenced how scientists and mathematicians study the multitude of nonlinear systems in our world, including how our heart beats, how the economy sometimes functions and how complex weather patterns behave.

Her programming work, physicists say, would make her a co-author today, because programmers are charged with writing the computable code that scientists need to run simulations they design. But fuller credit was not provided until Thierry Dauxois, a French physicist, championed her contributions in a 2008 article in Physics Today titled “Fermi, Pasta, Ulam, and a Mysterious Lady.”

“Her programming of a 1950s computer was not a trivial task,” he wrote. “Why has her contribution received only a two-line acknowledgment?”

Soon afterward, the problem became more widely known as Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou. And despite the intriguing headline in the Physics Today story, she told The Los Alamos Monitor, a local newspaper, that she was far from “mysterious.”

Mary Tsingou, the younger of two daughters, was born to Greek immigrant parents in Milwaukee on Oct. 14, 1928. The Tsingous moved during the Depression to Bulgaria, where they had property, before returning to Milwaukee in 1940, soon after the start of World War II.

Her father, Thomas Tsingou, was a factory worker, and her mother, Anastasia Koutsouyianni, had only a second-grade education. Her parents spoke Greek at home, and it was well into their childhoods before Mary and her sister, Sally, had fluency in English.

Back in Milwaukee public schools, the daughters were so behind in English that they were initially held back several grades — yet both were so strong in math that they were soon able to resume education at grade level.

In 1951, Mary Tsingou received a bachelor’s degree from the University of Wisconsin with the intent of becoming a high-school math teacher.

In her oral history, she said school jobs were sparse for women, because male veterans returning from the Korean War were given priority. She learned that Los Alamos was hiring women to do hand computing, which was considered a clerical job mostly reserved for women. She and the others in her cohort were informed that they would be paid less than the men doing the same work.

She temporarily left Los Alamos to work on a master’s degree in mathematics and received her diploma from the University of Michigan in 1955. Over the years, her mathematical and code-writing skills were used in thermonuclear research and for the Strategic Defense Initiative, the Reagan-era antimissile system popularly known as Star Wars.

In 1958, she married Joseph Menzel, who worked in security at Los Alamos. He died in 2022. In addition to Ann, she is survived by another daughter, Carol Menzel; eight grandchildren; and three great-grandchildren.

Reflecting on her career, Ms. Menzel said in the Los Alamos lab publication that she was not bothered by being left out of the 1955 experiment’s original name, Fermi-Pasta-Ulam.

“I was just doing the job,” she said. “I was glad to get paid.”

Mary Tsingou Menzel as a young mathematician. She joined what was then Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory in 1952.

Credit...Los Alamos National Laboratory
